# Dalan

> Dalan runs a bot or a web app from a home computer with no public IP and no server. The home program makes only outbound long-polling calls to Dalan; people use Dalan's web app ({site}) with a verified mobile number; Dalan passes messages between them. Its servers are inside the country, so it keeps working when links to the outside world are down.

## Connect a Telegram bot (no code change)

Dalan speaks the Telegram Bot API (snapshot 10.4). Change only two things in an existing bot:

- Server address: {api} (calls go to {api}/bot<token>/<method>, like Telegram)
- Token: the Dalan token of the bot (create it below)

Served: getMe, getUpdates (long polling; webhooks are not served), sendMessage with reply and inline keyboards, editMessageText, editMessageCaption, editMessageReplyMarkup, deleteMessage, pinChatMessage, unpinChatMessage, unpinAllChatMessages, answerCallbackQuery, setMyCommands, getMyCommands, deleteMyCommands, sendPhoto, sendDocument, sendAudio, sendVideo, sendVoice, getFile, setMyProfilePhoto (a static picture, PNG, JPEG or WebP, becomes the bot's icon), removeMyProfilePhoto, sendChatAction, deleteWebhook. Any other method answers ok=false with a clear description.

Formatting: `parse_mode` "HTML" works with Telegram's tags (b, i, u, s, tg-spoiler, a, code, pre, blockquote); `entities` and `caption_entities` work too. "MarkdownV2" and "Markdown" are not parsed: the text shows as sent.

Replies: `reply_parameters` (or `reply_to_message_id`) makes a reply; a user's reply reaches the bot with `reply_to_message`.

A keyboard button may have `style` (`success`, `danger` or `primary`; another value is a 400). A reply keyboard keeps `is_persistent`, `resize_keyboard` and `one_time_keyboard`. An inline button with `switch_inline_query`, `switch_inline_query_current_chat` or `switch_inline_query_chosen_chat` puts `@bot query` in the user's input (Dalan has no inline mode). `duration` (seconds) on sendVoice, sendAudio and sendVideo is kept and shown.

A bot never gets a user's phone number, only id, name and username.

## Core API (without Telegram)

Header on every call: `Authorization: Bearer <bot token>`. Base: {api}

- `GET /v1/updates?offset=<last update_id + 1>&timeout=30` long polls (the server cuts a timeout over its maximum). An update is confirmed by the next call's offset. Each update has `update_id` and a `message` (`id`, `from` {`id`, `name`, `username`}, `text`, `date`, and `reply_to` {`id`, `from`, `text`} when it replies) or a `callback`.
- `POST /v1/messages` with JSON `{"user_id": 5, "text": "Hi"}` sends a message. Optional: `reply_keyboard` (rows; a button is a text or `{"text": "Yes", "style": "success"}`), `reply_keyboard_persistent`, `reply_keyboard_resize`, `reply_keyboard_one_time`, `inline_keyboard` (a button has `callback_data`, `url` or `switch_query`, and may have `style`), `entities` (Telegram's, like `[{"type": "bold", "offset": 0, "length": 2}]`), `reply_to` (a message id), and `duration` (seconds) with a voice, audio or video file.
- `PATCH /v1/messages/<user_id>/<message_id>` with `text`, `entities` and `inline_keyboard` edits a bot message (`text` is the caption of a file message).
- Errors are JSON `{"error": "<code>", "message": "<what went wrong and how to fix it>"}`.

A user message waits for the bot only a short time (`update_expiry_seconds` in {site}/api/public/settings); after that it is marked "not delivered". Keep the bot polling.

## Get an access key (for agents and the CLI)

A person who is an approved builder logs in at {site}, opens "Account", and makes an access key in the "AI agents" part. The key starts with `dalan_`, is shown once, and expires. It can only create bots, rotate tokens and read bot status. It cannot read chats. Never put a key or a bot token in a repository.

## MCP server

URL: {site}/api/mcp (Streamable HTTP, stateless). Header: `Authorization: Bearer <access key>`.

Tools: `list_bots`, `create_bot` (username, name), `rotate_token` (bot_id), `bot_status` (bot_id), `set_bot_icon` (bot_id, image_base64: PNG, JPEG or WebP).

Claude Code:

    claude mcp add --transport http dalan {site}/api/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $DALAN_KEY"

Other agents: add an HTTP MCP server with the same URL and header.

## CLI

One Node file (Node 18 or newer, no packages), served by Dalan itself:

    curl -O {site}/dalan.mjs
    export DALAN_URL={site} DALAN_KEY=dalan_...
    node dalan.mjs bots
    node dalan.mjs create weather_bot "Weather"
    node dalan.mjs token <bot id>
    node dalan.mjs status <bot id>
    node dalan.mjs icon <bot id> <image file>

Output is JSON on stdout (exit 0). An error is JSON on stderr (exit 1). A wrong command prints the usage (exit 2).

## REST for builders

Base {site}, header `Authorization: Bearer <access key>`:

- `GET /api/builder/bots`: your bots
- `POST /api/builder/bots` with `{"username": "weather_bot", "name": "Weather"}`: a new bot and its token (shown once)
- `POST /api/builder/bots/<id>/token`: a new token; the old one stops at once
- `GET /api/builder/bots/<id>`: one bot with `online` and `last_seen`
- `PUT /api/builder/bots/<id>/icon` with the image as the body (PNG, JPEG or WebP, small): sets the icon; `DELETE` removes it. `GET /api/bots/<id>/icon` shows it to anyone (use `?v=<icon_version>` for caching)

A bot username is 5 to 32 characters of a-z, 0-9 and _, starting with a letter.

## Run a web app (site)

An approved builder shows a web app that runs on their own computer at `https://<name>.<sites domain>` with the Dalan agent. The app stays unchanged; the agent makes only outbound calls.

    curl -fsSL {site}/install.sh | sh              (Windows: irm {site}/install.ps1 | iex)
    dalan login <access key>
    dalan http 3000 --name mysite                  try it: online while the terminal is open, Ctrl+C stops it
    dalan service install                          keep it online in the background, also after a restart
    dalan status                                   the service and each site, online or offline
    dalan service uninstall                        stop the service and remove it

- On Windows the service is the user's Run key: it starts at log-on (not at boot) and is not started again after a crash. Log: `%APPDATA%\dalan\dalan.log`. Linux: `journalctl --user -u dalan`; macOS: `~/Library/Logs/dalan.log`.

- `GET /api/sites`: your sites with `online`; `POST /api/sites` with `{"name": "mysite"}` reserves a name (3 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and -).
- Answers stream, so Server-Sent Events work. WebSocket from the visitor to the app does not work yet.
- The real visitor address is in `X-Forwarded-For`; the app is reached as `Host: localhost:<port>`, the site's name is in `X-Forwarded-Host`.

## Login with Dalan (OpenID Connect)

A site of Dalan can let its visitors log in with their Dalan account. Two ways; guide for people: {site}/guide/login.

1. The proxy does it (no code): in "My apps" turn on "Require login on the proxy" for the site, or run `dalan http 3000 --name shop --login`. A visitor with no login goes to Dalan's login and back. Every request then reaches your app with `X-Dalan-User` (the user's id for this site) and `X-Dalan-Name` (the name, percent-encoded UTF-8). A visitor cannot send these headers themselves. A call that is not a page load (POST, fetch) with no login gets 401. `/.dalan/logout` on the site logs out.
2. OpenID Connect in your app (any library): in "My apps" turn on "Login with Dalan" for the site and copy the secret (shown once; "New secret" replaces it).

    issuer / discovery    {site}  ->  {site}/.well-known/openid-configuration
    client_id             the site name, for example shop
    client_secret         from My apps
    redirect_uri          https://shop.<sites domain>/... or http://localhost:<port>/... for tests
    flow                  authorization code with PKCE (S256, required); client_secret_basic or client_secret_post
    scopes                openid (needed), profile (name, preferred_username), email (email, email_verified, only when the user ticks it)

- The `sub` is different for each site, so two sites cannot match their users. A site never gets the phone number.
- The code works once and only for a short time; the ID token and access token (for `{site}/oauth/userinfo`) are short too. There are no refresh tokens: keep your own session after login.
- Errors come back to `redirect_uri` as `error=access_denied` (the user said no) or `error=invalid_request` (no PKCE). A wrong return address is refused on Dalan's own page.
- The user sees and removes the sites they allowed in "Login and security"; the next login then asks again.
